text:
alex: Heads-up: saw a regression on the fused-attn path when we enabled epilogue fusion + QKV packing + bias/rope fusion together on the 8k benchmark.

maria: ugh, details? batch size / seq len?

alex: baseline = flash_attn_v2 (no epilogue fusion). test config: bs=8, seq=8192, model=redwood-7b-like, kv-caching enabled, kv page size=1024.

alex: perf numbers from perf-bench:
```
baseline (flash_attn_v2):  token/s = 420
qkv-packing only:      token/s = 480  (+14%)
bias+rope fused only:  token/s = 510  (+21%)
all fused (epilogue+qkv+bias+rope): token/s = 380 (-9% vs baseline)
```

jordan: interesting — enabling all fusions drops perf. stack traces or kernels hot?

alex: profiler shows kernel time shifted: small kernels (epilogue) get a lot longer, plus more L2 spills on SM due to register pressure. aggregated time: epilogue kernel + memory prep increased by ~35%.

kevin: sounds like register pressure / spilling. qkv packing reduces compute but increases per-thread regs if we inline bias/rope logic. did you check occupancy numbers?

alex: yeah. occupancy dropped from 80% -> 52% for epilogue kernel. Spill stores increased 2.6x.

sophia: KV cache behavior might amplify this: when paging KV with 1024 blocks, we do more pointer math in the epilogue to merge cached KV pages. Could be causing the complexity increase.

maria: hypothesis: qkv pack + bias/rope fusion increases register live ranges, pushing epilogue into lower occupancy. possible fixes: 1) split epilogue into two kernels (compute-heavy + write-back) 2) compiler hints / restrict pointers 3) limit fusion (only do bias/rope fusion when seq < threshold)

jordan: can we get a microbench for the epilogue kernel with and without KV paging? bench-bot, run micro on sm=90, bs=8, seq=8192, kv_page=1024, kernels: epilogue_fused vs epilogue_sep

bench-bot: queued: epilogue_micros (epilogue_fused, epilogue_sep) on sm90. will post results in ~20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kevin: also add a run with disabled rope fusion (keep qkv pack + bias only). want to see which fusion combo is the main culprit.

alex: added that. bench-bot queued another 3 runs (qkv+bias, qkv+rope, bias+rope).

bench-bot: results: epilogue kernel micro (avg of 50 iters):
```
epilogue_sep (no fusion):  48.2 us
epilogue_qkv_only:       44.1 us
epilogue_bias_rope:      41.0 us
epilogue_all_fused:      66.5 us  <-- big regression
```

maria: confirms the fused-all path is bad. epilogue_all has more register spills according to nvprof.

kevin: NVTX traces? any unexpected memcpy or syncs?

alex: no extra syncs. it's purely compute/register pressure. local variables in fused kernel grew ~+18 registers.

sophia: interesting tradeoff: fusing reduces global memory accesses for bias/rope but increases per-thread storage. For long sequences with KV paging, the memory working set of the kernel interacts badly with shared mem usage for page lookups. Might oversubscribe shared mem + registers -> spills.

jordan: temporary mitigation: change kernel-selection heuristic: prefer epilogue-separated when seq >= 4096 OR kv_page_count > 4 OR estimated_regs > threshold. That way we keep qkv/bias/rope fusion for short sequences where it helps.

maria: agree. add a cost model: predicted_regs = base_regs + pack_regs + rope_regs + bias_regs + kv_page_regs(k). if predicted_regs > 64 -> pick separated epilogue. We already have compile-time regs estimate for kernels; just need to sum them.

alex: i'll instrument the kernel selector to emit reason codes and a histogram. then run end-to-end to validate tradeoffs.

kevin: also file a task to consider splitting epilogue: compute-only then write-back smaller kernel; that reduces live ranges. Might be more consistent across configs.

sophia: note: we should also run with different batch sizes; bs=1 vs bs=8 vs bs=16 could change register allocation. Add bs sweep to the bench.

bench-bot: queued: param sweep bs in [1,4,8,16], seq in [1024,4096,8192], kernel variants (sep, qkv, bias_rope, all). ETA 2h.

maria: for the release branch let's gate auto-fusion behind a new flag `enable_epilogue_fusion_v2` default=false until we validate heuristics. safer to ship conservative.

alex: agreed. I'll open PR: "runtime: selective epilogue fusion heuristic + telemetry" with tests and perf gating.

jordan: reminder: add a regression test that runs the 8k kv-paged scenario in CI perf job (smoke) to catch this.

alex: will do. Also capturing nvprof slices and a small repro script in the PR for reviewers.

kevin: great writeup. tl;dr: full fusion isn't always better; watch register pressure + KV paging interactions. heuristics + potential epilogue split are next steps. :thumbsup:

sophia: thanks. please @-mention me on the PR for design review.

alex: will do. posting the initial perf logs + nvprof dump here: https://internal.redwood/bench/1764209876-epilogue-fusion-logs

maria: nice. closing loop once sweep finishes and PR lands.

bench-bot: sweep complete. summary: for seq>=4096 and bs>=8, "all_fused" is slower in 87% of combos. for seq<=1024, "all_fused" wins ~65% of combos. detailed csv attached.

alex: perfect. thanks everyone. next: PR + telemetry + CI regression check.
